Perpetuity

per-puh-TOO-i-tee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Perpetuity is the quality or state of lasting forever, without end.

The city council debated whether the statue's inscription should promise the park would remain public in perpetuity.

Worked Example

The land was set aside in perpetuity as a nature preserve, meaning no future owner could ever develop or sell it.

Perpetuity emphasizes that something is meant to continue without any planned end -- often used in legal or financial language.

How Perpetuity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

eternity

eternity: infinite or unending time

permanence

permanence: the state of lasting indefinitely without change

Antonyms

impermanence

impermanence: the state of lasting only a short or limited time

transience

transience: the quality of being brief or temporary

How Strong Is It? — durability → eternity → perpetuity

durability vs. perpetuity

durability vs. perpetuity: Durability simply means something can withstand wear over time, without the absolute, unending scope of perpetuity.

eternity vs. perpetuity

eternity vs. perpetuity: Eternity pushes even further than perpetuity, describing time with literally no beginning or end at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — perpetu-

root — perpetu-: continuous, never ceasing (Latin perpetuus)

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state of, quality of (Latin/French)

Put it together

Put it together: Perpetuity comes from Latin perpetuus ('continuous, never ceasing'), the same root behind the everyday word perpetual, plus -ity ('state of') -- 'the state of being perpetual,' or lasting forever.

Use the root in a new word: perpetual

Use the root in a new word: perpetual: The old clock tower was said to run on a perpetual motion machine that never needed winding.
